column1: # Negative terms — phrases that CANCEL an explicit root.
# Format:  term<TAB>weight     (sign is ignored; always applied as negative)
# Every entry here exists because a real, innocent page would otherwise be
# blocked. The scorer sums positives and negatives, so a page about nationality
# law picks up `جنس` from `الجنسية` and immediately loses more than it gained.
# Rule for adding one: name the page you are keeping reachable. If you cannot
# name it, the fix belongs in the positive list (a more specific term) rather
# Keeps: passport renewal, visa applications, naturalisation law, any consular
# page. This is the highest-traffic false positive in Arabic and the reason the
# short root `جنس` carries a low weight.
# Keeps: ministry-of-health pages, medical references, school curricula, and
# reporting on sexual violence — all of which use the clinical vocabulary.
# Keeps: NHS/CDC/Mayo pages, biology coursework, and journalism.
# --- English: words whose innocence is purely contextual --------------------
# Keeps: naval and security reporting ("escort carrier", "police escort"),
# art history ("nude study"), and fashion retail ("lingerie department").
# Every entry names a page it keeps reachable. German compounds make this
# especially load-bearing: `Nacktschnecke` is a slug, `Nacktmull` a naked
# mole-rat, and `Sexualkunde` is what the subject is called in school.
# `geil` is youth slang for "great"; `Schwanz` an animal's tail; `blasen`
# bubbles; `spritzen` an injection; `reifen` tyres. These cancel the low
# weights those words carry in terms.de.tsv.
